overview: Black hits the b4 pawn with 1...c5. If White takes with 2.bxc5, Black can regain with ...e6 and ...Bxc5, getting the centre while White has spent a tempo; White can also play 2.Bb2 cxb4 or 2.b5. It is sound for Black and not really a gambit. I am not sure of the main branch.

white_ideas.idea: Take on c5, then Bb2 and develop with a pawn up temporarily
Fianchetto with Bb2 and play for the long diagonal
Play 2.b5 or Bb2 and keep a flank set-up

black_ideas.idea: Regain the c5 pawn with ...e6 and ...Bxc5, getting a good centre
Play ...Qa5 or ...Nf6 to hit the b-pawn

typical_structures.structure: White flank set-up with a pawn on b4 or b5 against a Black centre
Black c-pawn exchanged and Black has d- and e-pawns in the centre

character.notes: Flank play with unbalanced pawns but no early forcing play.

gambit.notes: White takes on c5 and Black normally regains with ...Bxc5 at once, so no material is lost by force. I tag it none.

soundness.notes: Sound; gives Black no problems and White no edge.

structure.notes: Neither side has a fixed centre; flexible.

approach.notes: The Polish is a surprise weapon used rarely by strong players; offbeat.

level.notes: Plans are flank-oriented and not very difficult.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2.Bb2
sublines_that_differ.how: White offers the b-pawn instead of taking on c5.

character.reason: Flank play with unbalanced pawns but no forcing lines.

gambit.reason: The pawn on c5 comes back easily after ...e6 and ...Bxc5.

approach.reason: The Polish is a surprise weapon for strong players.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes on b2 and plays on the queenside.
